stem: The value of escape velocity of a body from the earth's surface is \(V_{esc} =\) ______.
solution: The escape velocity is the minimum velocity needed to project a body so that it escapes the earth's gravitational field. Equating kinetic energy to gravitational potential energy, \(\frac{1}{2}mV_{esc}^2 = \frac{GMm}{R}\), giving \(V_{esc} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}}\). Correct option: C.

stem: In ______ of the modern periodic table, are the non-metals found.
solution: Non-metals occupy the right-hand side of the modern periodic table (Groups 13 to 18, except some metals/metalloids), which belongs to the \(p\)-block. The \(s\)-block and \(d\)-block, \(f\)-block contain metals. Correct option: B.

stem: The resistance of the wire is \(100\ \Omega\). If it is carrying a current of \(1\ A\) for \(10\) seconds, the heat produced will be ______.
solution: By Joule's law of heating, \(H = I^2 R t = (1)^2 \times 100 \times 10 = 1000\ J\). Correct option: D.

stem: The refractive index of diamond is ______.
solution: Diamond has the highest refractive index among common materials, \(2.42\); this large value is why light undergoes strong bending and total internal reflection in it, giving diamond its sparkle. (1.54 is glass, 1.36 is alcohol, 1.50 is a typical glass value.) Correct option: A.

subtopic: Human Eye and Defects of Vision
stem: For normal human eye, the minimum distance of distinct vision is ______.
solution: The least distance of distinct vision for a normal human eye is \(25\) cm — the nearest distance at which the eye can see an object clearly without strain. Correct option: C.

stem: Find odd man out: Cooking of food, Ripening of fruit, Milk turned into curd, Transformation of ice into water.
solution: Odd man out: Transformation of ice into water. Cooking of food, ripening of fruit and milk turning into curd are chemical changes (new substances are formed and the change is irreversible), whereas the transformation of ice into water is only a physical change (change of state; no new substance is formed and it is reversible).

stem: By observing the correlation in the first pair, complete the second pair: Mass : Kilogram : : Weight : ______.
solution: Newton. The SI unit of mass is the kilogram, and the SI unit of weight (which is a force, \(W = mg\)) is the newton (N).

stem: State whether the following statement is true or false: 'The volume of water at \(4\ ^{\circ}\)C is maximum'.
solution: False. Due to the anomalous behaviour of water, the volume of a given mass of water is minimum (and its density is maximum) at \(4\ ^{\circ}\)C, not maximum.

stem: What is the wavelength of violet ray in dispersion of light?
solution: The wavelength of violet light is about \(400\) nm (\(4000\) angstrom), which is the shortest wavelength in the visible spectrum. Because of this shortest wavelength, violet light is refracted (deviated) the most during dispersion.

stem: Give scientific reason: The geostationary satellites are not useful for studies of polar regions.
solution: A geostationary satellite revolves in an orbit that lies in the equatorial plane of the earth, at a height of about \(35780\) km, with a period of \(24\) hours so that it appears stationary over one point on the equator. From this equatorial position it can view mainly the equatorial and mid-latitude regions; the polar regions lie almost edge-on and are not properly covered. Hence geostationary satellites are not useful for studying the polar regions — for that, polar (sun-synchronous) satellites in low polar orbits are used.

stem: Give scientific reason: The hydrogenation of vegetable oil in presence of nickel catalyst forms Vanaspati-ghee.
solution: Vegetable oils are unsaturated compounds — they contain carbon–carbon double bonds (\(C = C\)). When such oils are heated with hydrogen gas in the presence of a nickel catalyst, an addition reaction takes place and the double bonds get saturated (converted to single bonds): \(C = C + H_2 \xrightarrow{Ni} C - C\). The saturated product is a semi-solid fat. Hence the hydrogenation of vegetable oil in presence of nickel catalyst forms Vanaspati-ghee.

stem: Give scientific reason: Atomic radius goes on increasing down the 'group'.
solution: On going down a group, a new shell (energy level) is added at every step, so the number of shells increases. As a result the distance of the outermost electrons from the nucleus increases, and the inner shells also screen (shield) the outer electrons from the nuclear pull. Even though the nuclear charge increases, the effect of the added shells and shielding dominates, so the outermost electrons are held less tightly. Hence the atomic radius goes on increasing down a group.

stem: What is meant by an 'alloy'? Give two examples.
solution: An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more metals, or of a metal with a small quantity of a non-metal, prepared to obtain desired properties (such as greater hardness, strength or resistance to corrosion). Examples: (1) Brass — an alloy of copper and zinc; (2) Steel — an alloy of iron and carbon. (Bronze, an alloy of copper and tin, is also acceptable.)

stem: Distinguish between oxidation and reduction.
solution:
| Oxidation | Reduction |
|---|---|
| Addition of oxygen (or an electronegative element) to a substance. | Removal of oxygen (or an electronegative element) from a substance. |
| Removal of hydrogen (or an electropositive element) from a substance. | Addition of hydrogen (or an electropositive element) to a substance. |
| Loss of electrons by a species. | Gain of electrons by a species. |

For example, in \(2Cu + O_2 \rightarrow 2CuO\), copper is oxidised; in \(CuO + H_2 \rightarrow Cu + H_2O\), copper oxide is reduced.

stem: Give the molecular formula and structural formula of Benzene.
solution: Molecular formula of benzene: \(C_6H_6\). Structural formula: benzene is a cyclic (aromatic) hydrocarbon in which six carbon atoms form a regular hexagonal ring with alternate single and double bonds (\(C = C\) and \(C - C\)) between adjacent carbons, and one hydrogen atom attached to each carbon. It is usually drawn as a regular hexagon of six carbon atoms with three alternate double bonds (often represented by a hexagon with a circle inside to show the delocalised bonds).

stem: An electric tungsten bulb is connected into a home circuit. The home electric supply runs at \(220\) volt potential difference. When switched on, a current of \(0.45\ A\) flows through the bulb. What must be the power (wattage) of the bulb? If it is kept 'on' for \(10\) hours, how many units of electricity will be consumed?
solution:
Power of the bulb: \(P = V \times I = 220 \times 0.45 = 99\ W\). So the wattage of the bulb is about \(99\) W (nearly \(100\) W).

Energy consumed in \(10\) hours \(= P \times t = 99\ W \times 10\ h = 990\ Wh = 0.99\ kWh\). Since \(1\) unit of electricity \(= 1\ kWh\), the electricity consumed \(= 0.99\) unit (approximately \(1\) unit).

stem: 'A rainbow is the combined effect of refraction, dispersion and total internal reflection of light'. Explain the sentence.
solution: A rainbow is seen after rain when tiny water droplets remain suspended in the atmosphere and the sun is behind the observer. Each raindrop acts like a tiny prism and produces a rainbow through three effects: (1) Refraction and dispersion — when sunlight (white light) enters a droplet it bends (refracts) and splits into its seven constituent colours because different colours are refracted through different angles (dispersion). (2) Total internal reflection — these dispersed colours strike the inner back surface of the droplet at an angle greater than the critical angle and are totally internally reflected inside the drop. (3) Refraction again — as the colours leave the droplet they are refracted (and further dispersed) once more. The combined effect of these many droplets sends the separated colours to the observer's eye, forming the coloured arc of the rainbow (red on the outside, violet on the inside).

stem: How much time a satellite in an orbit at height \(35780\) km above earth's surface would take, if the mass of the earth would have been four times its original mass?
solution:
The period of a satellite is \(T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{r^3}{GM}}\), where \(r\) is the orbital radius (unchanged, since the height is the same) and \(M\) is the mass of the earth. A satellite at height \(35780\) km is a geostationary satellite, so its original period is \(T = 24\) hours.

If the mass of the earth becomes four times, \(M' = 4M\), then
\(T' = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{r^3}{G(4M)}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{4}} \times 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{r^3}{GM}} = \dfrac{T}{2}\).

Therefore \(T' = \dfrac{24}{2} = 12\) hours. The satellite would take \(12\) hours to complete one revolution.

Observe the figure (apparatus in which acetic acid is dropped through a thistle funnel onto sodium carbonate in a big test tube, and the gas evolved is passed through a gas delivery tube into a small test tube containing freshly prepared lime water) and answer the following questions:
(a) Which gas is released out as effervescence in the big test tube?
(b) What is the colour change in the lime water?
(c) Write the related chemical equation.
solution:
(a) The gas released as effervescence is carbon dioxide (\(CO_2\)).
(b) The freshly prepared lime water turns milky (colourless lime water changes to milky white), because insoluble calcium carbonate is formed.
(c) Related equations:
Reaction in the big test tube: \(Na_2CO_3 + 2CH_3COOH \rightarrow 2CH_3COONa + H_2O + CO_2\uparrow\).
Reaction with lime water: \(Ca(OH)_2 + CO_2 \rightarrow CaCO_3\downarrow + H_2O\) (the white \(CaCO_3\) makes the lime water milky).

stem:
Read the following paragraph and answer the questions:
If heat is exchanged between a hot and cold object, the temperature of the cold object goes on increasing due to gain of energy and temperature of the hot object goes on decreasing due to loss of energy. The change in temperature continues till the temperatures of both the objects attain the same value. In the process, the cold object gains heat energy and the hot object loses heat energy. If the system of both objects is isolated from environment by keeping it inside a heat resistant box, then no energy can flow from inside the box or come into the box.
(a) Heat is transferred from where to where?
(b) Which principle do we learn from this process?
(c) How will you state the principle briefly?
solution:
(a) Heat is transferred from the hot object (at higher temperature) to the cold object (at lower temperature), until both attain the same temperature.
(b) We learn the principle of heat exchange (principle of calorimetry / method of mixtures).
(c) Principle of heat exchange: When a hot object and a cold object are kept in contact in an isolated system, the heat energy lost by the hot object is equal to the heat energy gained by the cold object, i.e. heat energy lost by hot object \(=\) heat energy gained by cold object.

stem: Draw a neat labelled diagram of electric motor and write its principle.
solution:
Labelled diagram (to be drawn by the candidate): a rectangular coil ABCD placed between the curved poles (N and S) of a permanent magnet; the two ends of the coil connected to a split ring (commutator) whose halves press against two carbon brushes; the brushes connected through a battery and a switch. Labels: armature coil, permanent magnet poles (N, S), split-ring commutator, brushes, battery, axle.

Principle: When a current-carrying conductor (coil) is placed in a magnetic field, it experiences a mechanical force given by Fleming's left-hand rule. The forces on the two opposite sides of the coil act in opposite directions, producing a torque (turning effect) that makes the coil rotate continuously. Thus an electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical (rotational) energy.

stem:
\(2NaOH + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow Na_2SO_4 + H_2O\)
State whether above chemical reaction is balanced or not. From the number of atoms present in the reactants and products, fill in the blanks:

| Elements | Reactants (Left Side) No. of atoms | Products (Right Side) No. of atoms |
|---|---|---|
| Na |  | 2 |
| O |  |  |
| H |  |  |
| S | 1 |  |
solution:
Counting atoms of the given equation \(2NaOH + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow Na_2SO_4 + H_2O\):

| Elements | Reactants (Left Side) | Products (Right Side) |
|---|---|---|
| Na | 2 | 2 |
| O | 6 | 5 |
| H | 4 | 2 |
| S | 1 | 1 |

The number of O atoms (6 vs 5) and H atoms (4 vs 2) are not equal on the two sides, so the reaction as written is NOT balanced. It is balanced by putting the coefficient 2 before water: \(2NaOH + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow Na_2SO_4 + 2H_2O\) (then O \(= 6 = 6\) and H \(= 4 = 4\) on both sides).

(b) Non-metals in the third period.
(c) Two elements having valency 4.
solution:
(a) Metalloid in the second period: Boron (B); metalloid in the third period: Silicon (Si).
(b) Non-metals in the third period: Phosphorus (P), Sulphur (S) and Chlorine (Cl).
(c) Two elements having valency 4: Carbon (C) and Silicon (Si).

stem:
Study the entries in the following table and rewrite them by putting the connected items in the single row:

| I | II | III |
|---|---|---|
| (a) Weight | \(\mathrm{m/s^2}\) | zero at the centre |
| (b) Acceleration due to gravity | \(\mathrm{N\,m^2/kg^2}\) | Same in the entire universe |
| (c) Gravitational constant | \(\mathrm{N}\) | Changes from place to place |
solution:
The correctly connected rows are:

| I | II | III |
|---|---|---|
| (a) Weight | \(\mathrm{N}\) | Changes from place to place |
| (b) Acceleration due to gravity | \(\mathrm{m/s^2}\) | zero at the centre |
| (c) Gravitational constant | \(\mathrm{N\,m^2/kg^2}\) | Same in the entire universe |

Reasons: Weight \(W = mg\) is a force, unit newton (N), and it changes from place to place because \(g\) varies. Acceleration due to gravity \(g\) has unit \(\mathrm{m/s^2}\) and is zero at the centre of the earth. The universal gravitational constant \(G\) has unit \(\mathrm{N\,m^2/kg^2}\) and has the same value everywhere in the universe.

stem: What is meant by 'mirage'? In which condition mirage is seen? Give such one more example.
solution:
Mirage is an optical illusion in which a distant object (such as a tree or the sky) appears to be reflected as if from a sheet of water on the ground. It is caused by the continuous refraction and finally total internal reflection of light passing through layers of air of different densities (temperatures).

Condition: A mirage is seen on hot summer days over a tarred road or a desert. The air close to the hot ground is hotter and less dense (optically rarer), while the air above is cooler and denser. Light from the sky travelling downward bends more and more away from the normal as it passes from denser to rarer layers, and at a certain layer undergoes total internal reflection, so the sky appears like a shimmering pool of water on the road.

One more example of such an atmospheric-refraction effect: the sun is seen a little above the horizon (and appears before actual sunrise and after actual sunset) due to atmospheric refraction. (The twinkling of stars is another acceptable example.)

stem:
(a) Draw a diagram of 'image formed by concave lens'.
(b) State the nature of image formed by concave lens.
(c) If the focal length of a concave lens is \(25\) cm, find the power of the lens.
solution:
(a) Ray diagram (to be drawn by the candidate): For an object placed anywhere in front of a concave (diverging) lens, one ray parallel to the principal axis diverges as if coming from the principal focus \(F\) on the same side as the object, and a second ray through the optical centre goes straight. The refracted rays appear to meet on the object's side, forming the image between the focus \(F\) and the optical centre — the image is virtual, erect and diminished.
(b) Nature of image formed by a concave lens: it is always virtual, erect (upright) and smaller than the object (diminished), and is formed on the same side of the lens as the object.
(c) For a concave lens the focal length is negative: \(f = -25\ \text{cm} = -0.25\ \text{m}\). Power \(P = \dfrac{1}{f\ (\text{in metre})} = \dfrac{1}{-0.25} = -4\ D\). The power of the concave lens is \(-4\) dioptre (negative, since it is a diverging lens).

stem:
(a) Write the main steps in the extraction of aluminium.
(b) What is the melting point of alumina and how is the melting point reduced?
(c) Why anodes need to be replaced from time to time during the electrolysis of alumina?
solution:
(a) Main steps in the extraction of aluminium: (1) Concentration/purification of the ore bauxite to obtain pure alumina \((Al_2O_3)\) — the Bayer's process; (2) Electrolytic reduction of molten alumina (the Hall–Heroult process) to obtain aluminium metal at the cathode.
(b) The melting point of pure alumina \((Al_2O_3)\) is very high, about \(2050\ ^{\circ}\)C. This melting point is reduced by dissolving the alumina in molten cryolite \((Na_3AlF_6)\) along with a little fluorspar \((CaF_2)\); this mixture melts at about \(950\)–\(1000\ ^{\circ}\)C and also becomes a good conductor of electricity.
(c) During the electrolysis of molten alumina, the oxygen liberated at the anode reacts with the hot carbon (graphite) anodes to form carbon dioxide gas: \(C + O_2 \rightarrow CO_2\). Because of this, the carbon anodes are gradually oxidised (burnt away) and become thinner, so they have to be replaced from time to time.
